note: M114 evidence for public-derive-from-behavior-v5: 34 one-expression string functions from 25 permissively licensed repos (MIT / Apache-2.0; GPL, AGPL, unlicensed and NOASSERTION repos were dropped). Each entry is re-derived by deriveStringProgram from a seeded grid of input lines built from its own tokens and delimiters (seed 114): the first 6 grid rows, then only the rows the refusals asked for (every asked row of a round answered by the upstream function itself), else the next grid row, at most 40 rows; the derived program is then checked against the upstream function on every other grid row and on 400 probe rows from strProbeTable. 30 in-vocabulary functions derive with 0 wrong on 12806 held-out rows. 4 entries are marked outOfVocabulary on purpose (trimStart before a two-character prefix, `.pop() || path`, `split()[1] || "main"`, `slice(1)`): 1 is refused (derive_no_fit) and 3 derive an in-vocabulary program that agrees with every example but is wrong on some held-out rows (wrongAt lists the first three). This is the disclosed out-of-vocabulary limit: v5 misses no in-vocabulary rival fit, but it cannot know a function outside its vocabulary. Upstream text, commit, path, git blob sha and sha256 of the fetched file are recorded per entry.
